context.title: The Families Who Returned
context.summary: A register lists those who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua by family and hometown — people, priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers and temple servants — about 50,000 in all, with their animals and gifts.
context.background: Records of family and town mattered: they showed who belonged to Israel and who could serve as priests. The listed family numbers add up to fewer than the stated total of 42,360 (v. 64); the difference may include people not itemized. Nehemiah 7 repeats this list with small differences.

customs.note: A Persian title for the governor.
Sacred lots kept in the high priest's breastpiece for seeking God's decision. Their use apparently had lapsed.

watchFor: Priests who could not prove their descent were kept from the priesthood (vv. 61–62).

w: the [ones who] had had themselves enrolled

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.summary: In the Babylonian orthography Nabu-kudur-uzur, which means “Nebo, protect the crown!” or the “frontiers.” In an inscription he styles himself “Nebo’s favourite.”

people.name: Zerubbabel
people.summary: The seed of Babylon, the son of Salathiel or Shealtiel (Hag. 1:1; Zorobabel, Matt. 1:12); called also the son of Pedaiah (1 Chr. 3:17-19), i.e., according to a frequent usage of the word “son;” the grandson or the nephew of Salathiel.

people.name: Joshua
people.summary: The son of Jozadak, and high priest of the Jews under Zerubbabel (Neh. 7:7; 12:1, 7, 10, 26); called Joshua (Hag. 1:1, 12; 2:2, 4; Zech. 3:1, 3, 6, 8, 9).

people.name: Rehum
people.summary: One of “the children of the province” who returned from the Captivity (Ezra 2:2); the same as “Nehum” (Neh. 7:7).

people.name: Seraiah
people.summary: A priest of the days of Jehoiakim (Neh. 12:1, 12).

people.name: Baanah
people.summary: Father of Iteleb, one of David's mighty men.

people.name: Bigvai
people.summary: In my body.

people.name: Bilshan
people.summary: Son of the tongue; i.e., “eloquent”, a man of some note who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:2; Neh. 7:7).

people.name: Mispereth
people.summary: Number, one of the Jews who accompanied Zerubbabel from Babylon (Ezra 2:2); called also Mispereth (Neh. 7:7).

people.name: Mordecai
people.summary: One of the leaders of those who returned from exile with Zerrubabel in the days of Cyrus.

people.name: Nehemiah
people.summary: Ezra 2:2; Neh. 7:7.

people.name: Reelaiah
people.summary: Thunder of the Lord, one of the princes who returned from the Exile (Neh. 7:7); called also Reelaiah (Ezra 2:2).

people.name: Parosh
people.summary: Ramiah.

people.name: Shephatiah
people.summary: Ezra 2:4.

people.name: Arah
people.summary: 652 children.

people.name: Pahath-moab
people.summary: Governor of Moab, a person whose descendants returned from the Captivity and assisted in rebuilding Jerusalem (Ezra 2:6; 8:4; 10:30).

people.name: Jeshua
people.summary: Ezra 2:6; Neh. 7:11.

people.name: Joab
people.summary: Ezra 2:6.

people.name: Zattu
people.summary: Id., one whose descendants returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:8; Neh. 7:13); probably the same as Zatthu.

people.name: Zaccai
people.summary: Pure, one whose “sons” returned with Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:9; Neh. 7:14).

people.name: Bani
people.summary: One of David's thirty-seven warriors.

people.name: Bebai
people.summary: The descendants of Bebai.

people.name: Adonikam
people.summary: Whom the Lord sets up, one of those “which came with Zerubbabel” (Ezra 2:13).

people.name: Bigvai
people.summary: Head of Jewish family.

people.name: Adin
people.summary: Ezra 8:6.

people.name: Ater
people.summary: Ezra 2:16.

people.name: Hezekiah
people.summary: Babylon.

people.name: Bezai
people.summary: Head of a Jewish family, which returned from Babylon.

people.name: Jeshua
people.summary: Head of the ninth priestly order (Ezra 2:36); called also Jeshuah (1 Chr. 24:11).

people.name: Jedaiah
people.summary: Knowing Jehovah.

people.name: Immer
people.summary: The head of the sixteenth priestly order (1 Chr. 24:14).

people.name: Pashur
people.summary: Son of Malchiah.

people.name: Harim
people.summary: The head of the second course of priests (1 Chr. 24:8).

people.name: Kadmiel
people.summary: Before God; i.e., his servant, one of the Levites who returned with Zerubbabel from the Captivity (Neh. 9:4; 10:9; 12:8).

people.name: Asaph
people.summary: A Levite; one of the leaders of David’s choir (1 Chr. 6:39). Psalms 50 and 73-83 inclusive are attributed to him. He is mentioned along with David as skilled in music, and a “seer” (2 Chr. 29:30).

people.name: Akkub
people.summary: A Levite who kept the gate of the temple after the return from Babylon (1 Chr. 9:17; Ezra 2:42; Neh. 7:45).

people.name: Shallum
people.summary: A keeper of the gate in the reign of David (1 Chr. 9:17).

people.name: Talmon
people.summary: A Levite porter (1 Chr. 9:17; Neh. 11:19).

people.name: Ater
people.summary: Ezra 2:42.

people.name: Hatita
people.summary: Exploration, one of the temple porters or janitors (Ezra 2:42).

people.name: Shobai
people.summary: Captors (Ezra 2:42).

people.name: Hasupha
people.summary: Uncovered, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:43; Neh. 7:46).

people.name: Tabbaoth
people.summary: Impressions; rings, “the children of,” returned from the Captivity (Ezra 2:43).

people.name: Ziha
people.summary: The name of a family of Nethinim (Ezra 2:43; Neh. 7:46).

people.name: Akkub
people.summary: The head of one of the families of Nethinim (Ezra 2:45).

people.name: Hanan
people.summary: One of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:46).

people.name: Gahar
people.summary: Lurking-place, one of the chief of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:47).

people.name: Giddel
people.summary: His sons were temple servants.

people.name: Reaiah
people.summary: Giddel.

people.name: Nekoda
people.summary: Father of Rezin.

people.name: Rezin
people.summary: King of Damascus,.

people.name: Uzza
people.summary: Paseah.

people.name: Mehunim
people.summary: Habitations, (2 Chr. 26:7; R.V. “Meunim,” Vulg. Ammonitae), a people against whom Uzziah waged a successful war. This word is in Hebrew the plural of Ma’on, and thus denotes the Maonites who inhabited the country on the eastern side of the Wady el-Arabah.

people.name: Harhur
people.summary: Fever, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:51).

people.name: Harsha
people.summary: Worker or enchanter, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:52; Neh. 7:54).

people.name: Barkos
people.summary: Painter, (Ezra 2:53; Neh. 7:55).

people.name: Sisera
people.summary: The ancestor of some of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:53; Neh. 7:55).

people.name: Hatipha
people.summary: Captured, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:54).

people.name: Neziah
people.summary: Victory; pure, Ezra 2:54; Neh. 7:56.

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Perida
people.summary: One whose descendants returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:55); called also Perida (Neh. 7:57).

people.name: Jaala
people.summary: A wild she-goat, one of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned from the Captivity (Neh. 7:58).

people.name: Delaiah
people.summary: The head of one of the bands of exiles that returned under Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:60; Neh. 7:62).

people.name: Tobiah
people.summary: Delaiah.

people.name: Barzillai
people.summary: A priest who married a daughter of the preceding (Ezra 2:61).

people.name: Koz
people.summary: A descendant of Judah.

places.name: Babylon
places.summary: The Greek form of BABEL; Semitic form Babilu, meaning “The Gate of God.” In the Assyrian tablets it means “The city of the dispersion of the tribes.”

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Bethlehem
places.summary: A city in the “hill country” of Judah. It was originally called Ephrath (Gen. 35:16, 19; 48:7; Ruth 4:11). It was also called Beth-lehem Ephratah (Micah 5:2), Beth-lehem-judah (1 Sam. 17:12), and “the city of David” (Luke 2:4).

places.name: Netophah
places.summary: Distillation; dropping, a town in Judah, in the neighbourhood, probably, of Bethlehem (Neh. 7:26; 1 Chr. 2:54). Two of David’s guards were Netophathites (1 Chr. 27:13, 15).

places.name: Anathoth
places.summary: The name of one of the cities of refuge, in the tribe of Benjamin (Josh. 21:18). The Jews, as a rule, did not change the names of the towns they found in Palestine; hence this town may be regarded as deriving its name from the goddess Anat.

places.name: Azmaveth
places.summary: A town in the tribe of Judah, near Jerusalem (Neh. 12:29; Ezra 2:24).

places.name: Beeroth
places.summary: Wells, one of the four cities of the Hivites which entered by fraud into a league with Joshua. It belonged to Benjamin (Josh. 18:25).

places.name: Chephirah
places.summary: Village, one of the four cities of the Gibeonitish Hivites with whom Joshua made a league (9:17). It belonged to Benjamin.

places.name: Geba
places.summary: The hill, (2 Sam. 5:25 [1 Chr. 14:16, “Gibeon”]; 2 Kings 23:8; Neh. 11:31), a Levitical city of Benjamin (1 Kings 15:22; 1 Sam. 13:16; 14:5, wrongly “Gibeah” in the A.V.), on the north border of Judah near Gibeah (Isa. 10:29; Josh. 18:24, 28).

places.name: Ramah
places.summary: A city first mentioned in Josh. 18:25, near Gibeah of Benjamin. It was fortified by Baasha, king of Israel (1 Kings 15:17-22; 2 Chr. 16:1-6).

places.name: Michmas
places.summary: Something hidden, a town of Benjamin (Ezra 2:27), east of Bethel and south of Migron, on the road to Jerusalem (Isa. 10:28). It lay on the line of march of an invading army from the north, on the north side of the steep and precipitous Wady es-Suweinit (“valley of the little thorn-tree” or “the acacia”), and now bears the name of Mukhmas.

places.name: Ai
places.summary: One of the royal cities of the Canaanites (Josh. 10:1; Gen. 12:8; 13:3). It was the scene of Joshua’s defeat, and afterwards of his victory.

places.name: Bethel
places.summary: A place in Central Palestine, about 10 miles north of Jerusalem, at the head of the pass of Michmash and Ai. It was originally the royal Canaanite city of Luz (Gen. 28:19).

places.name: Nebo
places.summary: The “children of Nebo” (Ezra 2:29; Neh. 7:33) were of those who returned from Babylon.

places.name: Hadid
places.summary: Pointed, a place in the tribe of Benjamin near Lydda, or Lod, and Ono (Ezra 2:33; Neh. 7:37).

places.name: Ono
places.summary: A town of Benjamin, in the “plain of Ono” (1 Chr. 8:12; Ezra 2:33); now Kefr ‘Ana, 5 miles north of Lydda, and about 30 miles north-west of Jerusalem.

places.name: Jericho
places.summary: Place of fragrance, a fenced city in the midst of a vast grove of palm trees, in the plain of Jordan, over against the place where that river was crossed by the Israelites (Josh. 3:16).

places.name: Cherub
places.summary: Plural cherubim, the name of certain symbolical figures frequently mentioned in Scripture. They are first mentioned in connection with the expulsion of our first parents from Eden (Gen. 3:24).

places.name: Tel-harsha
places.summary: near the sea

places.name: Tel-melah
